rationale: `src/authoring/mod.rs#struct[PendingAssessment]` is a plain data holder. It carries the subject, the validated evidence `record`, the outcome and the usage log between the judgment and the write to its destination. It makes no decision, check or output that `requirements.authoring.persistence` specifies. The code that does the persistence is separately marked {impl}: `impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[persisted]`, `fn[configured_assessment]`, `fn[record]` and `impl[AuthoringSubject]/fn[evidence_path]` in the same file, and `fn[stage_record]` and `fn[persist_record]` in `src/authoring/batch.rs`. The struct is reached through those marked items and uses the types they use, so it needs no {impl} of its own. It is also not a test. It does depend on the requirement: it holds the record that is written as evidence, and the text names the subject, judgment and recorded inputs as what gets written. A change to that text could require changing the struct's fields. {cite} is therefore the right role. The struct has no {impl} or {test} reference to the same requirement, so the citation is not redundant.

text: After one valid judgment, the harness MUST write the subject text, submitted
determination and rationale, and recorded inputs using the existing evidence
By default, it MUST write the subject's evidence file. With `--stdout`, it MUST
emit a single evidence JSON object followed by a newline to stdout and MUST NOT
create or change evidence files or directories. All three outcomes MUST be
